names.citation: Constellation names, abbreviations and genitives: International Astronomical Union, "The Constellations", https://iauarchive.eso.org/public/themes/constellations/.

lines.citation: Constellation figures: Stellarium sky culture "modern_iau" (Stellarium team; figures after the IAU / Sky & Telescope constellation charts by Roger Sinnott, Rick Fienberg and Alan MacRobert), CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/Stellarium/stellarium.

boundaries.version: VizieR VI/49, CDS ReadMe history last entry 23-Jul-2024 (J2000 boundaries for CEP and UMI fixed.)
boundaries.citation: Constellation boundaries: Davenhall A.C., Leggett S.K. 1989, "Catalogue of Constellation Boundary Data", CDS VizieR VI/49 (1997yCat.6049....0D), after Delporte E. 1930, "Delimitation scientifique des constellations". This research has made use of the VizieR catalogue access tool, CDS, Strasbourg, France (DOI: 10.26093/cds/vizier).

conventions.frame: ICRS/J2000 equatorial; RA in degrees [0,360), Dec in degrees.
conventions.lines: [hipA, hipB] = one straight segment between two Hipparcos stars (deduplicated, undirected). Resolve 3-D positions with hip-index.json -> stars.bin, or sky positions with lineStars.
conventions.boundary: Array of rings; each ring = array of [raDeg, decDeg] vertices (J2000), implicitly closed (last vertex joins the first; first vertex not repeated). Vertices are <= ~1 deg apart (Davenhall & Leggett interpolation), so straight chords on the unit sphere are accurate. Rings may cross RA 0/360; Ursa Minor and Octans rings encircle the celestial poles. Serpens has two rings (boundaryParts SER1 = Caput, SER2 = Cauda).
conventions.label: labelRaDeg/labelDecDeg: derived anchor for the constellation name (see labelMethod), J2000.
conventions.areaDeg2: Derived solid angle of the boundary rings in square degrees (IAU values sum to 41253 deg^2).

lineStars.note: index/distPc null = star has no usable HYG distance (cannot be placed in 3-D).
